sentences.text: A chartplotter puts that GPS position on an electronic chart, and it’s the tool you’ll stare at most.
It shows where you are, on the chart, in real time.
You can drop waypoints and string them into a route.
The plotter draws a straight line between two waypoints.
Does it care what’s under that line?
It will happily route you across a shoal, or an island.
So zoom in and check every leg before you follow it.
Cross-track error tells you how far you’ve slid to one side of your intended track.
Watch it in a cross current.
Remember that vector charts hide detail when you’re zoomed out.
And keep the charts updated, and never rely on a single source.
The Coast Guard, and the courts, expect a prudent captain to cross-check the plotter against the buoys, the depth, and what he can see.
